skill.name: prompt-caching
skill.description: Guides LLM prompt caching, response caching, and Cache Augmented Generation decisions for lower cost, lower latency, and safer invalidation.
skill.summary: Helps design prompt, response, and CAG caching strategies for LLM applications.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown inline code in SKILL.md. I found no evidence of command execution, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent in the reviewed file.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 61 uses Markdown inline code to list related skill names. It does not instruct the model to run commands or execute shell content.

content.value_statement: Repeated prompts can increase latency and LLM spend. This skill helps teams choose prompt, response, and CAG caching patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Claude native prompt caching for repeated prefixes.
Compares prompt prefix caching, response caching, and semantic match caching.
Calls out cache invalidation risks and stale response problems.
Advises on CAG patterns that preload documents instead of retrieval.
Identifies anti-patterns such as high-temperature caching and caching everything.
limitations: Does not implement a cache store, SDK wrapper, or monitoring system.
Does not calculate provider pricing or guarantee savings.
Requires users to adapt strategies to model, temperature, and workload.
Does not replace current provider documentation for API parameters.

use_cases.title: Reduce Repeated Prompt Cost
use_cases.description: Plan prefix caching for shared instructions, tool schemas, and documents that repeat across calls.

use_cases.title: Design Response Cache Rules
use_cases.description: Define cache keys, freshness rules, and invalidation paths for repeated user requests.

use_cases.title: Evaluate CAG Versus RAG
use_cases.description: Compare preloaded document context with retrieval when documents are stable and frequently reused.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Caching Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Learning which caching pattern fits a new LLM workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the differences between prefix caching, response caching, and CAG for my application. Recommend the safest first step.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Claude Prefix Cache
prompt_templates.scenario: Improving prompts that repeat shared instructions or documents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt structure: [paste structure]. Identify stable prefixes, cache boundaries, and changes that reduce cache misses.

prompt_templates.title: Design Response Cache Policy
prompt_templates.scenario: Adding full response caching to repeated user requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a response caching policy for my workflow. Include cache keys, temperature limits, invalidation triggers, and monitoring signals.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Multi-Level Cache Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Reviewing a production design that uses several cache layers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this LLM caching design: [describe architecture]. Find risks across prefix, response, semantic, and CAG layers, then propose improvements.

output_examples.input: A support chatbot repeats a long policy manual in every request.
output_examples.output: Use prefix caching for stable policy text. Keep volatile user details later in the prompt to protect cache hits.

output_examples.input: A summarization service uses high temperature and caches full responses.
output_examples.output: Avoid full response caching for this path. Lower temperature or cache only deterministic stages with clear freshness rules.

output_examples.input: A team wants to preload stable documentation instead of retrieving it each turn.
output_examples.output: Consider CAG when documents are small enough, stable, and reused often. Add invalidation when the documentation changes.

best_practices: Keep stable instructions and documents at the beginning of prompts.
Cache deterministic or low-temperature responses with explicit freshness rules.
Measure hit rate, miss latency, stale responses, and cost before expanding scope.
anti_patterns: Caching high-temperature creative outputs as if they were deterministic.
Changing prompt prefixes on every request and expecting provider cache hits.
Caching sensitive or fast-changing data without expiration and invalidation.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps choose practical caching strategies for repeated LLM prompts, responses, and stable document context.

faq.question: Does this skill implement a cache?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance, tradeoffs, and review prompts for teams building their own cache layer.

faq.question: How does it help with Claude?
faq.answer: It explains repeated prefix patterns that can work with Claude prompt caching when prompts are structured consistently.

faq.question: Can Codex or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex and Claude Code can use it to reason about LLM cache design during development.

faq.question: When should I avoid response caching?
faq.answer: Avoid it for personalized, sensitive, fast-changing, or high-temperature outputs without strict freshness and privacy controls.

faq.question: What should I measure first?
faq.answer: Measure hit rate, miss latency, stale output rate, storage cost, and saved tokens before expanding cache scope.
